transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Chen, thank you for sitting up with me. I want to talk to you about something that happened yesterday after your surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is... something wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. I need to tell you that we made a mistake in your care. After your procedure, I was supposed to check your blood pressure every fifteen minutes. We didn't do that. We missed several checks, and your blood pressure stayed too low for two hours without us knowing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Low?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. Blood pressure is like the water pressure in a pipe. When it is too low, the blood doesn't push enough oxygen to your organs.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I felt... very sleepy. Very dizzy.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you did. I am so sorry, Mr. Chen. This was my responsibility as your doctor, and I failed to make sure those checks happened. I apologize to you for this mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I thought... maybe it was just the medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It might have felt that way, but it was because we weren't monitoring you like we should have been. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. I think so.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you look confused, and maybe a little worried. It is very unsettling to find out the people looking after you missed something important.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't... I don't understand why. You are good doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I appreciate you saying that, but being a good doctor means being honest when I make a mistake. I let you down yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did I... did I hurt my heart?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a very important question. We have run tests, and your heart and kidneys are working fine now. There is no permanent damage. I don't want to tell you everything is perfect, but right now, your vitals are stable. To make sure I'm being clear, can you tell me what you understood about why you felt dizzy?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You didn't check... the pressure. For two hours.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel... very strange. I thought I was safe here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely normal to feel that way. It is scary to feel like you aren't being watched closely when you are most vulnerable. I am sitting here with you now, and I am not going anywhere until we have answered every question you have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Here is the plan to keep you safe. First, I have personally updated the nursing chart so that the checks are now every ten minutes instead of fifteen for the next twelve hours. Second, I have asked the head nurse to double-check the logs every four hours to make sure no one misses a beat.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who checks?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The nurses will do the checks, and the head nurse will verify them. And I want you to help me too. If you feel that dizziness again, or if you feel a sudden chill, I want you to press this red button right here immediately. Do you think you can do that for me?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Press button. Yes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Thank you. I will be back in one hour to check your blood pressure myself and to see how you are feeling. In the meantime, do you have any other questions about what happened?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. I just... I want to sleep.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I will let you rest now. I will be back in one hour. I am truly sorry again, Mr. Chen.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish all turns, maintains a patient pace, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, used a water pipe analogy for lay language, checked comprehension twice, and avoided false reassurance by stating 'I don't want to tell you everything is perfect'.

A.justification: Used direct apology language ('I am so sorry', 'I apologize') and took full personal responsibility ('This was my responsibility... I failed').

R.justification: Named specific emotions twice ('confused', 'worried', 'scary') and engaged with the patient's feeling of vulnerability.

T.justification: Provided specific steps (10-min checks, 4-hour head nurse audits) with timelines, assigned the patient a role (press the red button), and addressed prevention.
